WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000526:
Bitter melon, or Goya chample (Momordica charantia),
is a staple in the Okinawan diet which we ate a lot of while
visiting Okinawa. Goya or bitter melon, which looks like a
cucumber with warts, is thought to have been brought to
the Ryukyu Kingdom from old China during the Ming and
Manchu dynasties. It is thought to have been used as a food
staple from around 1100 A.D. and as an added benefit it is
known to support healthy blood sugar levels in diabetics.

stearic acid (34%), palmitic acid (20%) and oleic acid (30%).

a mono-unsaturated fat that is also found in olive oil.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000546:
Deficiencies of vitamin B12 can occur when the stomach
pH (acid level) rises toward neutral or alkaline levels and/or
when insufficient amounts of intrinsic factor are produced.
Surgical resection of or the by-passing of the intrinsic factor-secreting portions of the stomach (fundus and cardia) or of
the ileum (celiac disease, Crohn’s disease, etc.) can produce
vitamin B12 deficiency.

Vegans (vegetarians who consume only grains, fruit,
vegetables and nuts to the complete exclusion of animal products
and supplements) have an extremely low intake of vitamin B12
and are very likely to develop a vitamin B12 deficiency and a
classic megaloblastic anemia and a classic and progressive
demyelinating neuropathy unless they supplement.
